# v2.0.0 — eight new skills, behaviour evals, and rules that hold with any model

## Breaking change

`doc-author` is renamed `documentation-author`, to match `documentation-review` and the full-word names of the other skills. Its behaviour is unchanged. Prompts and scripts that name `doc-author` stop finding it.

## Upgrade

1. Pull this release, then run `make update`. It installs `documentation-author` and removes old `doc-author` copies that came from this repository; it keeps your own skill or a link with that name.
2. Run `make status` to confirm no old copies remain.
3. Change any prompt or script that names `doc-author` to `documentation-author`, or `agent-skills:documentation-author` through the plugin.

## Roll back

1. Check out the previous release, `git checkout v1.1.2`, and run `make update`. It reinstalls `doc-author`.
2. Remove the `documentation-author` folders from your skills folders by hand, because v1.1.2 does not know that name. `make status` from this release lists where they are.

## Highlights since v1.1.2

- **Eight new skills**, for each step from a request to a release. Each works on its own:
  - `specification-author` and `specification-review`: testable specifications, and a review that checks them against the code
  - `decision-record-author`: decision records that supersede rather than rewrite
  - `change-plan-author` and `test-plan-author`: small reviewable steps, and tests planned from the specification rather than the code
  - `security-review`: runs the repository's scanners, then reads every changed line
  - `release-notes-author`: notes that lead with upgrade steps, migrations, and how to roll back
  - `skill-correction`: turns a correction into a failing eval case and the smallest fix
- **Behaviour evals.** `make skill-agent-evals` runs an assistant with tools in a fixture repository and grades what it reads, runs, and writes. Each case is a contract that names no assistant, run through Claude Code or a built-in agent for llama.cpp, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible server. CI grades recorded runs and makes no model calls.
- **Rules that hold with any model.** Most skills bundle a checker that fails on what must not ship, and [Make a skill's rules hard](https://gautampachnanda101.github.io/agent-skills/hard-rules/) gives the assistant settings that enforce the rest.
- **Roles and owners.** Role pages show which skills each job uses. Every skill has an owner in `CODEOWNERS` and a level, and both are checked.
- **Suggest before asking.** Every skill now reads the repository first and sends one batch of suggestions, each with its evidence, for you to accept or correct. `backstage-catalog-builder` ranks owner signals (descriptors, `CODEOWNERS`, catalog groups, maintainers) and flags placeholder owners such as `group:default/catalog-test`.
- **Verified downloads.** `make skill-llm-verify` checks SHA-256 digests for the pinned llama.cpp archives and a revision-pinned model. It no longer ignores `LLAMA_CPP_URL`, `LLAMA_BUILD`, or `LLM_MODEL_URL` when a cache exists. CI runs it on Linux x64 and arm64 and macOS arm64 and Intel.
- **Real evals.** `make skill-evals` grades every skill with any model command. The review skills use a real diff and real pages with planted defects and clean companions. Answer keys are never sent to the model. A run that matches no case, or gets a bad argument, now fails instead of reporting success.
- **Stricter report graders.** They read the severity and evidence columns, enforce risk order, and check that verdicts agree with findings.
- **Pinned CI inputs.** The Claude Code CLI used for manifest validation is pinned, and the local-model cache key follows the pins.
- **Repository checks.** Every commit and CI run now lints Markdown (markdownlint) and shell scripts (shellcheck), audits the workflows (zizmor), and scans for secrets (gitleaks; CI scans the full history). Every GitHub Action and pre-commit hook is pinned to a commit, and Dependabot proposes updates after a week's cooldown.
- **Versions and releases are checked.** A changed skill must raise its version and update the changelog. A person publishes each release with `scripts/release.mjs` once `Verify` passes.
- **Decision records** in `docs/decisions/` explain why the repository works as it does.

## Eval results

All twelve skills pass their reply and behaviour evals with Claude Opus 5.5, and every reply case fails without its skill. [Verification](https://gautampachnanda101.github.io/agent-skills/verification/) has every result, including smaller local models.

The original four skills, three runs per reply case with the skill and one without:

| Skill | With the skill | Without |
| --- | --- | --- |
| backstage-catalog-builder | 6/6 | 1/2 |
| documentation-author | 5/6 | 1/2 |
| documentation-review | 6/6 | 0/2 |
| peer-code-review | 5/6 | 0/2 |

The two failures were then worked through with `skill-correction`. The `TODO` was a real gap, fixed in `documentation-author` 2.1.0 (two of six to three of three). The review had reported the duplication; the answer key was too narrow, and was fixed.

## Correction to v1.1.2

The v1.1.2 notes reported 8/8 and 10/10 recall. Those fixtures showed only part of the change and included the answer key in the model's input, so the figures did not measure the skills. The results above replace them.
